verdicts.quote: No failure writes a partial batch.
Row errors identify logical CSV record numbers, counting the header as 1, when applicable. Error responses omit raw row data and credentials.
verdicts.missing: Whether all failing rows are reported or only the first, and what reason/message each carries beyond the status code.

verdicts.quote: Existing and within-file email comparisons are case-insensitive. A conflict returns 409.
The baseline has no write endpoint or role model ... A configured server-side bearer token identifies an admin for this operation.
Accept name and email headers in either order, with case and surrounding whitespace normalized. ... Bad headers ... return 400.
verdicts.missing: What counts as a bad header: whether extra/unexpected columns are rejected or ignored, and explicit handling of a missing header row.

verdicts.quote: CSV supports CRLF and LF, a UTF-8 BOM, escaped quotes and quoted commas/newlines.
No failure writes a partial batch. ... incomplete or rejected request leaves the user store as observed before this request.
verdicts.missing: Side effects beyond store writes (e.g. invitations) are not addressed; whether any exist or are deferred until commit.

verdicts.quote: Accept up to and including 256 KiB and 1,000 data records. Exceeding either returns 413.
Bad headers, malformed CSV or UTF-8, empty imports ... return 400.
verdicts.missing: Whether 'empty imports' covers both a zero-byte file and a header-only file, and explicit single-row behaviour.

verdicts.quote: Replaying hits the existing email conflict at record 2 and leaves five records.
commits synchronously, and responds. ... There is no asynchronous completion or derived state.
No throughput or hosted availability commitment is defined.
verdicts.missing: No time bound for a maximum-size file; progress visibility is not addressed (only implied moot by synchronous response).

verdicts.quote: Preserve public GET list and ID lookup, seeded records, response shapes and 404 for unknown IDs. ... An overlapping conflict or replay leaves the existing set intact.
